mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 1000-rep walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite a statistically significant positive regression coefficient for the (UNRATE lagged 1mo) * (PAYEMS month change) interaction in a 200-day rolling OLS.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a sustained drop in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates a supply-side shock that outpaces demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 5% in a month while CPIAUCSL decreases by > 2% over the same period
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 50-rep bootstrap.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the ratio of industrial production to GDP (INDPRO/GDP) over three consecutive months suggests weakening aggregate supply capacity, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) in a 200-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (i.e., rates are rising), the discount rate applied to future earnings is expected to increase, reducing the present value of equity expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
regime_hint: normalization after a rate cut cycle
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of such events (rolling quantile).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding increase in employment (PAYEMS lagged) indicates an overheating labor market, which can trigger a short-term equity sell-off reflected in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month compared to the prior month while PAYEMS 1mo ago is flat
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in a 1000-rep walk-forward simulation.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the consumer price index followed by a sustained rise in retail sales (PAYEMS) suggests demand is recovering faster than inflation, which can support equity valuations and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by > 1% over two months while PAYEMS increases by > 3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 80% of similar regime windows (rolling quantile).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of declining industrial production (INDPRO) and rising unemployment (UNRATE), the supply-side fundamentals weaken, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) in a 50-day rolling window.
